primitives.name: Perceptron Convergence Theorem (Theorem 1)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Suppose the perceptron algorithm is run on a linearly separable data set D with margin γ > 0. Assume that ||x|| ≤1 for all x ∈D. Then the algorithm will converge after at most 1/γ² updates.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: k = number of perceptron weight updates (dimensionless integer count, k≥0). γ = margin of the separating hyperplane on dataset D, measured in activation units of w·x+b; under the book's normalization ||x||≤1 and a unit-norm optimal separator w*, γ is a dimensionless feature-space length with γ>0. The bound 1/γ² is therefore a dimensionless update count. x∈R^D are feature vectors normalized so ||x||≤1 (dimensionless after normalization); w (weights) and b (bias) carry activation units; labels y∈{−1,+1} are dimensionless. Source: Theorem 1, p.45; proof pp.45–46. Note: the draft's final proof line prints k≤1/√γ (a typo); the theorem statement and the margin note ('once we've made 1/γ² updates, we cannot make any more') give the correct k≤1/γ².
primitives.assumptions: Dataset D is linearly separable with strictly positive margin γ>0 (p.45); every example obeys the unit-norm bound ||x||≤1 (p.45); updates follow the error-driven rule w←w+yx, b←b+y, triggered exactly when ya≤0 (Algorithm 5, p.39). The proof posits existence of a unit-norm maximum-margin separator w* (p.45). The text notes the bound generalizes to ||x||≤R as an exercise (p.46).
primitives.breakdown_regime: If D is not linearly separable the perceptron never converges — 'the perceptron has no hope of converging' (p.44). As γ→0 the bound 1/γ² diverges, so razor-thin margins require quadratically many corrections. Convergence does NOT yield the maximum-margin separator: 'The data may be separable with margin 0.9 and the perceptron might still find a separating hyperplane with a margin of only 0.000001' (p.46). A fixed, non-permuted example order can make practical convergence astronomically slow even on separable data (pp.40–41).

layer2.mapping: Map the error-driven hyperplane learner onto a coach's play-call tendency model in the 22-player dynamical system. State x = per-snap feature vector (down, distance, field zone, personnel, formation, score/time context); label y = binary play success (e.g. positive EPA or conversion). Each failed call is a misclassification that triggers a tendency update w←w+yx, exactly the perceptron correction. The margin γ is the robustness buffer of the offense's success boundary in this feature space: a wide-margin scheme (success robust to small perturbation) stabilizes its call sheet after few corrections, while a razor-thin-margin scheme (success hinges on one precise read) needs quadratically more corrections, per k≤1/γ². This is an isomorphism of the correction-count bound, not a claim that football originated the theorem.
layer2.telemetry: Calibrate from play-by-play + tracking: per-snap feature vectors and success labels; count observable between-week tendency shifts (proxy for update count k); estimate a margin proxy from the separation of success/failure feature distributions or calibrated classifier confidence. The true geometric margin γ is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from broadcast data alone; only proxies are observable. No sportsbook odds used.

primitives.name: Expected-Loss Formalization of Inductive Learning (Eq 1.1)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given (i) a loss function ℓ and (ii) a sample D from some unknown distribution D, you must compute a function f that has low expected error ϵ over D with respect to ℓ.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: ϵ = expected loss, the D-average of ℓ (units of ℓ: dimensionless for 0/1 loss, squared-label-units for squared loss). D = data-generating probability distribution over input/output pairs (x,y); a probability measure with dimensionless mass summing to 1. ℓ(y,f(x)) = loss of prediction f(x) against truth y, units chosen by the task (0/1 dimensionless; squared loss in [label]²). f = learned hypothesis mapping inputs to predictions; x = input example; y = label. Eq (1.1), p.15. Companion training error ϵ̂=(1/N)Σₙℓ(yₙ,f(xₙ)), Eq (1.2), p.16, a dimensionless empirical average.
primitives.assumptions: Training data is a random sample of input/output pairs drawn from D (p.15); future/test examples are drawn from the same D (stationarity); no parametric assumption on D's shape — 'we are not making any assumptions about what the distribution D looks like' (p.15); D itself is unknown and accessible only through samples. The i.i.d. reading is made explicit in Chapter 7 (pp.102–103).
primitives.breakdown_regime: ϵ is uncomputable because D is unknown; only the empirical ϵ̂ is observable, and memorization drives ϵ̂→0 without reducing ϵ (p.16). The guarantee collapses under distribution shift: hold-out/cross-validation estimates hold 'only if your test data really looks like your training data ... drawn from the same distribution' (p.62). Dependent samples (pixels within an image, words within a document) violate independence and inflate apparent performance unless folds are split at the image/document level (p.62).

layer2.mapping: Derive the engine's risk functional from the source triple (D,ℓ,f). D becomes the distribution over game states the Coach-Mind simulator samples; ℓ becomes the play-value loss the engine actually cares about (points/EPA-style cost, not win-rate headlines); f becomes the play-call policy. The kernel K:(D,ℓ,f)↦(game-state distribution, play-value loss, policy) carries the invariant that only expected loss over the true state distribution — never training-set memorization — is the objective. Its failure mode maps directly: halftime opponent adjustment or season-to-season rule change is distribution shift, so the engine must re-weight or refuse extrapolation rather than trust a stale fit.
layer2.telemetry: Held-out-week calibration: predicted vs realized outcome distributions per game-state bucket; calibration error and sharpness tracked on data never used for fitting. Sealed Tuesday baseline hashes (tau=0.42) are never overwritten; no post-cutoff leakage; no sportsbook odds as inputs. The true D is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE; only sampled game states are observable.

primitives.name: Bayes Optimal Classifier (Theorem 8, Eq 7.1)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Bayes Optimal Classifier f (BO) achieves minimal zero/one error of any deterministic classifier.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f^(BO) = Bayes optimal decision rule; x̂ = test input; ŷ = predicted label ranging over the discrete label space Y; D(x̂,ŷ) = true data-generating probability of the pair (dimensionless probability mass, summing to 1 over Y for fixed x̂); argmax selects the highest-probability label. Eq (7.1), p.101. Bayes error rate ϵ_Bayes = E_{(x,y)∼D}[y≠f_Bayes(x)] (Eq 10.8, p.147), a dimensionless probability in [0,1].
primitives.assumptions: Hypothetical access to the true distribution D (p.101); zero/one loss; optimality is stated against deterministic classifiers, with a stronger randomized-classifier result noted (pp.101–102); the label space Y is discrete.
primitives.breakdown_regime: D is never actually known, so f^(BO) is unimplementable and must be approximated by estimating D (p.102). The Bayes error rate is an irreducible floor no classifier can beat: with label noise 'there's no way that it can do better than 20% error on this data' (pp.139–140). Optimality holds only for zero/one loss, not for asymmetric or importance-weighted losses (Chapter 5).

layer2.mapping: The Bayes error floor is isomorphic to the irreducible aleatoric uncertainty of football outcomes: ball bounces, tipped passes, gusts, and referee variance set a nonzero error floor that even a perfect model of the game-state distribution cannot beat. The engine should therefore spend capacity on reducible error (scheme mismatch, missing features, mis-calibration) rather than chasing the floor. This binds to a constraint on the simulator's objective: effort allocated to a prediction task should be proportional to its reducible gap above the Bayes floor, not to the raw error number.
layer2.telemetry: Estimate the floor from repeat-situation outcome variance: bucket snaps by (down, distance, field zone, personnel) and measure the spread of realized outcomes within a bucket; that within-bucket variance lower-bounds achievable error. The true D and exact Bayes floor are LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE; only empirical bucket variance is observable. No odds inputs.

primitives.name: Curse of Dimensionality: Distance Concentration and the Porcupine Sphere (Eq 2.2)
primitives.verbatim_quote: As D grows, the average distance between points in D dimensions goes to 1! In other words, all distances become about the same in high dimensions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D = ambient dimension (dimensionless count). a,b = independent random points uniform on the unit hypercube [0,1]^D (dimensionless coordinates). ||a−b|| = Euclidean distance in unit-hypercube length units. avgDist(D) = expected pairwise distance (same length units); the text states it tends to 1 as D→∞. r = radius of the central blue hypersphere touching 2^D unit green hyperspheres, expressed in units of the green-sphere radius (dimensionless), r=√D−1 (p.33); for D≥10 it pokes outside the enclosing hypercube. Eq (2.2), p.34.
primitives.assumptions: Points are drawn uniformly and independently on the unit hypercube — the concentration claim is established for Uni_D (p.34); Euclidean metric; the porcupine construction assumes 2^D unit hyperspheres packed at hypercube corners (p.33).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Real data is not uniform: 'the data that we get is not uniformly distributed over the unit hypercube' (p.34), so distances do NOT concentrate on the MNIST/text histograms (p.34). Adding many irrelevant uniform features DOES force concentration and breaks KNN (p.54). KNN also fails under feature-scale mismatch (millimeters vs centimeters, p.28) because it weights every feature equally and cannot select relevant ones.

layer2.mapping: A 22-player tracking frame lives in a high-dimensional space (22×(x,y,vx,vy,orientation) ≈ 110+ coordinates per frame). Nearest-neighbor play retrieval — finding 'similar' historical plays to inform a call — is exactly the KNN setting, so it inherits distance concentration: in the raw high-dimensional space all plays look equidistant and similarity search degenerates. The porcupine effect warns that a cluster looking 'round' in a 2D projection need not be round in the full space. The binding constraint: prune/normalize features and reduce dimension before any similarity-based retrieval, or the retrieval kernel is uninformative.
layer2.telemetry: Histogram of pairwise distances between play embeddings before vs after feature pruning/normalization; effective dimensionality; held-out retrieval precision of similar-play lookup. Concentration is directly observable as a collapsing distance histogram; the uniform-distribution assumption is testable and typically rejected for real tracking data.

primitives.name: AdaBoost Adaptive Weighting and Reweighting (Algorithm 31)
primitives.verbatim_quote: As long as the weak learner does, indeed, achieve < 50% error, then α will be greater than zero. As the error drops to zero, α grows without bound.
primitives.latex: \alpha^{(k)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\frac{1-\hat\epsilon^{(k)}}{\hat\epsilon^{(k)}}, \qquad d^{(k)}_n = \frac{1}{Z}\,d^{(k-1)}_n \exp\!\left[-\alpha^{(k)} y_n \hat y_n\right], \qquad f(\hat x)=\mathrm{sgn}\!\left[\sum_k \alpha^{(k)} f^{(k)}(\hat x)\right]
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: α^(k) = vote weight of the round-k weak classifier (dimensionless; natural log of an odds ratio, units nats). ε̂^(k) = weighted training error at round k (probability in [0,1], dimensionless). d_n^(k) = importance weight of example n at round k, a probability distribution over examples (dimensionless, Σₙ d_n=1). Z = normalization constant enforcing Σd=1 (dimensionless). y_n, ŷ_n ∈{−1,+1} true/predicted labels (dimensionless). f^(k) = round-k weak hypothesis; sgn = sign function. Algorithm 31, p.152; α derivation and the 80/20 worked example, pp.152–153.
primitives.assumptions: Each weak learner achieves weighted error strictly below 50% on the current reweighted distribution (the weak-learning assumption, pp.151–152); the weak learner accepts weighted training data (p.152); labels are ±1; the final classifier is a weighted majority vote of the weak hypotheses.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If ε̂=0.5 then α=0 and the round contributes nothing; if ε̂>0.5 then α<0 and the vote is inverted — the weak-learning assumption is violated (p.152 discussion). As ε̂→0, α→∞, so one near-perfect (possibly noise-fitting) weak learner can dominate the ensemble. Boosting decision stumps reduces to a linear classifier optimizing exponential loss (p.154), inheriting linear-model limits and up-weighting noisy labels, which can drive overfitting.

layer2.mapping: Derive an ensemble-of-weak-tendency-models kernel for game-plan prediction. Each weak learner is a simple tendency rule barely better than chance on a slice; AdaBoost combines them into a strong predictor, reweighting so later learners focus on situations the current ensemble fails (third-and-long, red zone, two-minute). The vote weight α=½log((1−ε)/ε) is the calibrated confidence assigned to each rule, and the ε<0.5 condition is a hard gate: a slice where a rule is at chance earns zero vote, worse-than-chance earns an inverted vote. This binds the transition kernel that updates slice importance between fitting rounds.
layer2.telemetry: Per-slice weighted error rates ε̂; the resulting α weights; held-out-week calibration of the combined predictor. The weak-learning gate is directly testable per slice (ε̂<0.5). No sportsbook odds; evaluation strictly on held-out data per the cardinal rule (p.21).

reasoning_traces.think:
The perceptron convergence theorem is, at bottom, a statement about how expensive it is to correct a mistaken boundary. It says that if the world is linearly separable with margin γ, then error-driven correction terminates after at most 1/γ² updates. Read forward, this is a design constraint: the number of mistakes a learner must absorb before it stabilizes is controlled not by the size of the data but by the geometry of the target — specifically by how much slack the correct boundary has. A wide margin means a forgiving world in which a rough guess is quickly refined; a thin margin means a brittle world in which only a very precise boundary works, and the learner pays quadratically for that precision. Read backward, the theorem becomes a diagnostic instrument. If we observe a decision-maker who keeps correcting and never stabilizes, the theorem tells us to look for a thin or vanishing margin, or for a target that is not separable at all, rather than blaming the learner's effort. This bidirectional move — bound forward, diagnose backward — is the sovereign content, and it is pure learning theory due to Rosenblatt (1958), not a football artifact.

Now compile it into the 22-player system as an explicit isomorphism. A coach's play-call tendency is a boundary in a feature space of down, distance, field zone, personnel and formation, separating successful from unsuccessful calls. Each failed call is a misclassification that nudges the tendency, exactly w←w+yx. The margin is the robustness of the scheme: a offense whose success survives small perturbations of protection or coverage has a wide margin and a call sheet that settles quickly; an offense whose success hinges on one exact read has a thin margin and a call sheet that oscillates. The bound predicts that thin-margin schemes demand far more corrective experience before they stabilize, which is why a fragile scheme looks 'coachable' only after many repetitions.

But the expected-loss formalization (Eq 1.1) reminds us what the corrections are even for: minimizing expected loss over the true state distribution, not training error. A coach can drive his 'training error' to zero by memorizing what worked last week, yet that is precisely the memorization the book warns does not generalize. And the Bayes optimal classifier sets the floor: some snaps are irreducibly uncertain — a tipped ball, a gust — and no amount of correction beats that aleatoric floor. So the mature reading stacks three invariants: the margin bound tells you how many corrections stabilization costs; the expected-loss kernel tells you corrections must target the true distribution, not the last game; and the Bayes floor tells you when to stop correcting and accept irreducible variance. The failure mode is treating a thin-margin, distribution-shifted, noise-dominated problem as if it were a wide-margin stationary one — which is exactly when a coaching staff keeps installing fixes that never stick.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The theorem's own lineage is a historical scar: Rosenblatt's 1958 perceptron (cited p.45 and bibliography p.186) was followed by the XOR limitation, which the book says 'basically killed research in classifiers with linear decision boundaries for a decade or two' (pp.49–50). That winter is the hidden state that shaped the field's later turn to kernels and multi-layer networks. In the football Layer-2 reading, a coach's comfort call is the analogous scar artifact: a blown lead installs a loss-aversion prior that persists long after the original context changed, so the current call is explained by a past wound rather than a fresh expected-loss calculation. I do not claim the theorem originated in football; football is the mapped system, and the genealogy is the mechanism by which a past failure becomes a present hidden bias.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Under pressure the beliefs clash recursively. The coach's comfort call rests on a belief that a conservative call protects the lead; the defensive coordinator's tendency trap rests on a belief that the offense will indeed run, so he stacks the box; the quarterback's internal clock rests on a belief about how much time the protection will buy. Each agent models the others: the coach anticipates the DC's stack, the DC anticipates the coach's comfort, and the QB anticipates both while his clock ticks. The high-EV deep shot only exists if the QB's clock, the protection scheme, and the DC's coverage belief align. Modeling this as a fixed-point of mutual beliefs, rather than a single optimizer, is what lets the engine see why a call that is high-EV in isolation collapses when one agent's belief is wrong.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Physics and psychology veto the high-EV call. Even when the play-call model ranks a deep shot highest, the quarterback's biomechanical state — fatigue, prior axonal-shear exposure, a lengthened internal clock under pressure — degrades throw accuracy and decision speed, so the realized outcome distribution is far worse than the model's. The GSI layer therefore overrides the GSE layer: a physiologically compromised QB cannot execute the high-EV option, and the honest move is to down-weight or refuse it. Venue weather and turf add a second physical veto on footing and ball flight. The veto is cross-layer because a purely decision-theoretic optimum is rejected by a lower-level physical constraint, exactly as a mathematically optimal call is rejected when the body cannot deliver it.

reasoning_traces.think:
The second cluster of invariants governs representation and evaluation rather than correction. The curse of dimensionality is a warning about the geometry of similarity: in high dimensions, under a uniform distribution, all pairwise distances concentrate to the same value, so the only signal a nearest-neighbor method uses — distance — evaporates. The porcupine sphere makes the same point visually: the central sphere's radius grows as √D−1 and eventually pokes outside the box that contains the corner spheres, so intuitions trained in two and three dimensions actively mislead. Read forward, this is a constraint on any retrieval-based reasoning: before you ask 'which past situation is most like this one,' you must prune and normalize features, or the question is meaningless. Read backward, if a similarity search returns nonsense, the diagnosis is concentration or scale mismatch, not a lack of data. Crucially the book also bounds the damage: real data is not uniform, so concentration is a danger to be tested for, not a law that forbids learning.

AdaBoost supplies the constructive counterpart. Where a single weak rule is barely better than chance, the adaptive weighting α=½log((1−ε)/ε) turns a collection of such rules into a strong predictor, and the reweighting step focuses later rules on the situations the ensemble currently fails. The hard gate is the weak-learning assumption: at ε=0.5 a rule earns zero vote, and beyond it the vote inverts. This is a fail-closed discipline — a rule that cannot beat chance on the reweighted slice is silently excluded rather than allowed to poison the ensemble. Compiled into football, this is an ensemble of weak tendency models, each competent on a narrow slice, combined with calibrated confidence and focused on the hard cases (third-and-long, red zone). The reduction of boosted stumps to a linear classifier optimizing exponential loss also warns that the ensemble inherits linear limits and will up-weight noisy labels.

Both invariants are governed by the cardinal rule: never touch your test data. The expected-loss objective is only estimable on data drawn from the same distribution and never used for fitting; cross-validation and development splits exist precisely to tune without contaminating the final estimate. The book's own genealogy — Valiant's PAC framework (1984), Occam's razor (c.1320), Freund and Schapire's AdaBoost — is a lineage of making 'simple solutions generalize' precise. The failure mode this cluster vetoes is the seductive one: a high-dimensional similarity search that looks rich, an ensemble that looks powerful, and a reported score that looks impressive, all secretly fit on the evaluation rows. The discipline is to keep the held-out set sealed, to test for distance concentration before trusting retrieval, and to gate every weak rule at chance — because an honest refusal to claim a fit beats a fabricated one.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This cluster's lineage is the discipline of generalization made formal: William of Occam's razor (c.1320, quoted p.138) became the Occam's Bound theorem that simple solutions generalize; Valiant's PAC framework (1984, p.140) made 'probably approximately correct' precise; and Freund and Schapire's AdaBoost won the 2004 Kanellakis Award (p.139) for theory that changed practice. The historical scar underneath is overfitting itself — the student who memorizes past exams and fails the new one (p.20). That scar produced the cardinal rule 'never touch your test data' (p.21) and the whole train/development/test separation. In the engine, the same scar explains why sealed Tuesday baselines and held-out weeks exist: they are institutional memory of every time a fit was secretly scored on its own training rows.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The recursive clash here is between analyst, coach, and opponent. The analyst believes the tendency data reveals a stable pattern; the coach believes his own comfort call is unpredictable; the opponent believes he can decode the tendency and trap it. Each models the others' model: the analyst must anticipate that the coach will deviate precisely to avoid being decoded, and that the opponent will adapt to whatever pattern is exposed. A high-dimensional similarity search that ignores this recursion retrieves plays the opponent has already seen and countered. The AdaBoost gate mirrors the social gate: a tendency rule that the opponent has neutralized falls to chance and must earn zero vote. Theory of mind thus tells the engine which slices are still informative and which have been adversarially erased.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The veto in this cluster is epistemic and physical at once. Epistemically, any reported performance fit on its own evaluation rows is vetoed outright by the held-out discipline — a high score that violates the cardinal rule is not evidence, it is contamination, and the honest action is to refuse the claim. Physically, distance concentration vetoes a similarity-based call before it is made: if the feature space has not been pruned and normalized, the retrieved 'most similar' play is meaningless, so the call built on it is rejected regardless of its apparent EV. And the Bayes floor vetoes over-investment: once reducible error is exhausted, further fitting only memorizes noise. Each veto is a lower-priority layer (geometry, physiology, evaluation hygiene) overriding a higher-priority decision-theoretic recommendation.

universal_lens: A polymath audit lens for any predictive enterprise: separate memorization from generalization, measure robustness by margin rather than by raw fit, respect the irreducible error floor, and treat the geometry of your feature space as a first-class constraint. The book's through-line — that simple, well-regularized, honestly-evaluated models generalize — is a universal discipline that applies wherever a boundary is learned from finite samples, from medicine to markets to motion.
gsi_mapping: Into GSI's fluid/axonal-shear and bioenergetics frame: the margin is isomorphic to a tissue-load tolerance buffer — a wide margin is robustness to perturbation, a thin margin is a structure near failure that needs many corrective cycles. Distance concentration maps to high-dimensional clinical feature spaces where naive patient-similarity retrieval degenerates unless features are pruned and normalized. The Bayes floor maps to irreducible physiological variability that no intervention removes. AdaBoost's reweighting maps to adaptive rehab loading that concentrates on the movements a patient currently fails, gated at chance so ineffective drills earn zero weight. Clinical telemetry (load, shear exposure, recovery markers) calibrates each mapping.
gse_mapping: Into GSE's Coach-Mind simulator, deception, and DFS/portfolio tail risk: the expected-loss kernel is the simulator's objective over game-state distributions; the perceptron margin bounds how many corrections a tendency model needs to stabilize and quantifies deception robustness. AdaBoost is the ensemble of weak tendency models with a fail-closed chance gate. The Bayes floor sets the irreducible tail that portfolio construction must respect rather than chase. The cardinal rule enforces held-out engine evaluation and protects sealed Tuesday baselines. All artifacts are internal; no picks or public copy are produced from this lane, and no sportsbook odds are used as inputs.
